The chromatic number χ ​ ( G ) \chi(G) of a graph G G is the smallest k ∈ { 1 , 2 , … } k\in\{1,2,\dots\} such that G G is k k -colorable. Graph k k -coloring usually refers to the task of finding a proper k k -coloring of a graph, if one exists. In a coloring of a graph, we say that an edge is monochromatic if its endpoints have the same color. Approximate k k -coloring is the task of finding a k k -coloring of a graph such that the number of monochromatic edges is approximately minimized. One type of method for approximate k k -coloring is a local search method , in which we have some space 𝒮 \mathcal{S} representing potential k k -colorings and some loss function ℒ : 𝒮 → [ 0 , ∞ ) \mathcal{L}:\mathcal{S}\rightarrow[0,\infty) representing the penalty of each potential k k -coloring, and we attempt to find an element of 𝒮 \mathcal{S} with small loss by choosing some initial element s 0 ∈ 𝒮 s_{0}\in\mathcal{S} , then iteratively finding new elements s t s_{t} for t = 1 , 2 , t=1,2, and so on such that s t + 1 s_{t+1} is close to s t s_{t} under some metric on 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and ideally has smaller loss.
